question: In your research system, the web search subagent hits a timeout on one query. The web search subagent returns only the status "search unavailable" to the coordinator. The coordinator then cannot tell whether to retry, try a different query, or continue with other sources. What is the main problem with this way of reporting the error?

options.text: The subagent reports the failure at all, when it should return an empty result marked as success so the workflow keeps running.
options.reason: The guide calls silently suppressing errors by returning empty results as success an anti-pattern, because it hides the failure from the coordinator.

options.text: The status fails to stop the whole research workflow, which is the safe response whenever any single subagent fails.
options.reason: The guide calls terminating entire workflows on single failures an anti-pattern, because the coordinator can often recover or continue with partial results.

options.text: The subagent sends the error to the coordinator, when subagents should resolve every failure locally and never propagate any errors.
options.reason: The guide says subagents recover locally from transient failures but propagate errors they cannot resolve, together with what was attempted and partial results.

options.text: The generic status hides the failure type, the attempted query, and any partial results, so the coordinator cannot choose an informed recovery action.
options.reason: The guide says generic statuses like "search unavailable" hide valuable context, while structured error context lets the coordinator make intelligent recovery decisions.
